newsitem.title: GERMANY: No country can veto NATO expansion, Kohl says.
newsitem.headline: No country can veto NATO expansion, Kohl says.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that no outside country would be able to veto the proposed enlargement of NATO but efforts must be made to address Russian concerns about the alliance's planned expansion.
"No one, and I mean no one, will have a veto over which countries can join," Kohl told a news conference after a summit meeting with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

France has proposed a summit of four big NATO powers and Russia but Kohl said if such a meeting took place it would simply be an "ad-hoc meeting" and did not mean a new "directorate" of major powers had formed within the alliance.
He said only July's Madrid summit could decide on which of the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe would be invited to join the alliance.

"No talks before Madrid can come to any decisions," he said. But he added NATO was happy to discuss NATO enlargement with Russia, proving it was clear no one had the right of veto and the Madrid summit could not be postponed.
Paris has suggested French, German, British and U.S. leaders hold a summit with Russia in April to discuss the broad outlines of a deal which would be acceptable to all sides.
"The (Madrid) summit will have great consequences for all the participants and for Russia," Kohl said. "The mood there against NATO expansion is very strong."
Russia says NATO expansion is unacceptable as it would place members of a foreign military alliance along its borders.
Diplomats say Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are leading the field to win admission to NATO, with Romania and Slovenia close behind.
